questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a strong introduction in a research paper or project, as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: To list all references and sources upfront
To hook the reader and explain what the paper will cover
To include random facts unrelated to the topic

correct_answer.text: To hook the reader and explain what the paper will cover

questions.question_text: According to the chapter, what is a key tip for creating effective visual aids like charts or slides?

options.text: Cram as much data as possible into one visual
Use bright, clashing colors to grab attention
Keep it clear and simple with labeled elements
Avoid crediting sources for images or data used

correct_answer.text: Keep it clear and simple with labeled elements

questions.question_text: What is one way to build confidence when delivering an oral presentation, based on the chapter’s advice?

options.text: Read directly from your notes without looking at the audience
Practice multiple times in front of a mirror or by recording yourself
Speak as fast as possible to finish quickly
Avoid using any visual aids to keep focus on your words

correct_answer.text: Practice multiple times in front of a mirror or by recording yourself

questions.question_text: How should you respond to feedback or questions after a presentation, according to the chapter?

options.text: Get defensive and argue if someone critiques your work
Ignore questions you don’t know the answer to
Listen actively, stay calm, and answer honestly or ask for clarity
Dismiss feedback as unimportant to your project

correct_answer.text: Listen actively, stay calm, and answer honestly or ask for clarity
